sections.html: The “chocolate neon tetra”, Hyphessobrycon vilmae, is only rarely available. It requires the very same conditions as the well known “black neon tetra”, Hyphessobrycon herbertaxelrodi.
Hyphessobrycon vilmae originates from the upper reaches of the Rio Tapajós in Brazil.
The males of H. vilmae have a more intensive coloration and also white colours in the fins, which are lacking in females.

Like in many other tetras, golden specimens quite often appear in H. vilmae. Sadly this pretty coloration is not hereditary. It is the result of a harmless infection with skin-worms. These worms cannot reproduce in aquaria. They reach the sexually active stage only in birds that have eaten an infected fish. The fish infect themselves by eating the faeces of infected birds. So all golden tetras that appear in the trade are always wild-collected fish.
